newsitem.title: USA: Washington Post says sees H2 hurt by ad rev.
newsitem.headline: Washington Post says sees H2 hurt by ad rev.

text.p: The Washington Post Co said Tuesday second-half results would be adversely affected by the lack of political and Olympic advertising that benefited Post-Newsweek stations in late 1996, as well as the increased spending for expansion at the company's Kaplan Educations Centers unit.
The company also said that it would invest further in its cable and new media operations later in the year.

The company said that its strong first quarter performance, where operating earnings totaled $78 million, versus $50.2 million in the year-earlier period, was aided by strength in its print operations.

Newspaper division revenues, said the company, climbed eight percent, year-to-year, while newsprint costs declined by 21 percent. Advertising volume increased in both international and domestic versions of Newsweek, said the company, boosting revenues at the magazine 11 percent.
The company also said that a strong local economy helped produce favorable earnings.
